messages:
elena: quick follow-up from the runtime hotseat: top ask was clarity on batching/caching tradeoffs and kernel rollout strategy. dropping a recap and some concrete asks.

sam: appreciated. can we be explicit about adaptive batching windows? last meeting we mentioned a "dynamic window" but not the policy.

ja: current plan is heuristics-based adaptive batching: start 8ms, grow up to 60ms under low QPS, shrink to min under p50 latency pressure. will add a knob for per-route max-window.

matt: will that interact with Dedicated latency SLOs? i.e., customers on reserved capacity expect tighter tails.

ja: yes — Dedicated routes will get an enforced max-window of 12ms by default, configurable by the tenant. host routes keep the 60ms ceiling.

sam: caching: are we moving to TTL-only or adding an eviction-first model (LRU) for prefix caches? some personalization workloads blow up memory.

ja: we'll implement hybrid TTL+size-based eviction. default prefix-TTL 120s, but for high-cardinality personalization routes we'll default to 15s and enforce max-prefix-entries per worker. ticketed as KERN-487.

ana: ops question: how will we validate kernel ABI changes across GPU types? last time we saw a float32->fp16 mismatch on older drivers.

ja: kernel rollout will have staged ABI checks: 1) unit ABI checker (local), 2) cross-arch smoke (small-inputs) in canary, 3) perf regressions measured on p95/p99 and mem pressure. if ABI mismatch detected, automated rollback.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary request queued: kernel-abi-v3 on canary-hosted-eu and dedicated-us-west at 1909991370. Monitoring hooks: perf, correctness, mem-leak.

matt: two more things: (a) quantized fallback policy for low-memory hosts? (b) how do we surface quantization-induced quality drop to users?

ja: (a) fallback: runtime will prefer quantized variant when OOM risk > 70% per-host prediction; fallback toggles per-request for long contexts. (b) we'll add an opt-in console badge and a telemetry flag so customers can see % of requests served quantized + sample diffs.

elena: on quality detection, add a lightweight smoke eval that runs on a small prompt set post-canary. if ROUGE/QA metrics drop beyond threshold, block. also tag any rollout with a "quality note" in the release page.

sam: CI metric request: can we compute tokens-per-second and cost-per-1M-tokens in canary so product teams can see economics?

ja: yes, add metrics: median tps, p95 tps, and estimated cost/1M based on pricing table; emit as numeric labels in canary run.

matt: owners & next actions please.

elena: action items: - Sam: define per-route max-window config and doc sample (owner: sam, due: 3 business days). - Jia: KERN-487 prefix eviction + quantized-fallback tickets + perf targets (owner: jia, due: next sprint). - Ana/Ops: ensure canary includes hosted-eu + dedicated-us-west + one low-memory host (owner: ana, due: today). - Matt: draft "quality gating" checklist for releases (owner: matt, due: 48h).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: kernel-abi-v3 at 1909991380.

elena: thanks all. i'll paste these into the runtime roadmap doc and ping the owners. if you have follow-ups post-meeting, reply here and i'll keep the thread open for 24h. :white_check_mark:
